property_summary: For any deployment and inputs, the correct contract's owner() returns the stored owner address (set during initialize), whereas the mutant returns address(0) for at least some inputs — so owner() must equal the initialized owner address for all inputs, which the mutant violates.

For any (admissible) initializer caller address, after initialize(...) the reference contract's owner() returns the address that performed initialization (the stored owner) for all inputs, whereas the mutant returns address(0) (breaking the rule) for some inputs.

After initialize(...) is called by any non-zero EOA, the contract's owner() must return the initializer address for every admissible initializer; the mutant that always returns address(0) violates this (owner() != initializer) for those inputs.

For any non-zero initializer address that calls initialize(...), the reference stores that address as owner() (owner() == initializer) for all admissible inputs; the mutant that always returns address(0) will disagree for those inputs.

For any non-zero EOA initializer, after calling initialize(...) the contract's owner() returns that initializer address; the mutant that always returns address(0) will sometimes differ (owner() != initializer).

For any caller address, the reference contract's owner() returns the stored owner (set during initialize), whereas the mutant returns the caller (msg.sender) causing owner() to differ for callers other than the stored owner.

For every caller, the correct contract's owner() returns the fixed stored owner (set at initialize), whereas the mutant returns the caller (msg.sender) — so for any caller equal to the stored owner the values match, but for some caller different from the stored owner the mutant will return a different address causing the property to fail.

For every caller address x, calling owner() should always return the stored owner (the address set during initialize) — the mutant returns msg.sender for some callers and thus will differ when the caller is not the stored owner.

For any caller address A, C.owner() always returns the stored owner (the address set during initialize); the mutant returns msg.sender instead, so when called by an address different from the stored owner the returned value differs.

For every caller address, the correct contract's owner() view returns the stored owner address (set during initialize); the mutant returns msg.sender, so when owner() is called by any address different from the stored owner the return values differ.

For every state of the contract, paused() returns the stored _paused flag (i.e., paused() == pausedFlag); the mutant flips the returned boolean, breaking this equality for inputs where _paused differs from its negation (i.e., when _paused is true or false — the fuzzer will find a state where the flipped return differs).
